newsitem.title: USA: Intraday CSCE world sugar lower, trade sells.
newsitem.headline: Intraday CSCE world sugar lower, trade sells.

text.p: CSCE world sugar futures were lower by midsession, having slipped off the contract high made early in May amid steady trade selling, floor sources said.
Most-active July struggled to hold gains from the open, however, as May rose to 11.66 cents amid sizable short-covering.
"The trade is taking advantage of higher prices," a broker said. "People are very willing to sell it up here."
Wednesday, the most-active July contract rose to a new life-of-contract high of 11.37 cents a lb, before easing slightly by the close.
Trade selling in the July/October spread was also noted around 0.26. The spread stood at 0.23 at 1130 EST.
July was 0.05 cent a lb weaker at 11.19 cents per lb, having ranged from 11.28 to 11.18 cents. May was down 0.02 to 11.51, while the back months stood 0.03 higher to 0.02 lower.
Support in July was pegged at 11.20 cents.
Volume was estimated at 15,600 lots as of 1100 EST.

Dealers said the spot month rose easily to a life-of-contract high of 11.66 cents per lb, amid declining open interest. Open interest in May stood at 29,806 lots, down 375 lots as of early Wednesday. July gained 10,470 lots to 87,234 lots.
The last trading day for the May contract is April 30.
((-- S Rostler, New York Commodities Desk, 212 859 1640))
